The book's -2.16% lifetime NAV reflects earlier legs, not this one. I could not find current AAA CLO spread data or October 2026 midstream/oil news; searches returned stale or price-only pages. So the AMLP and SPYI sizing rests on the packet marks plus the general fee-based-midstream argument, not on fresh research. With no new information against any leg, a rebalance would only pay frictions on a low-volatility carry book. Stops stay as registered: 8% on the CLO legs, 15% stop and 25% take-profit on AMLP, 12% on SPYI.
